title: build --local-sandbox fails from a git worktree, and so do two unit tests
foundBy: session agent, running `make check` from a git worktree while fixing SBX-044
details:
`make check` failed in a checkout made with `git worktree add`. Two tests were the failures, `TestLocalModuleProxyInstallsAnUnpushedRevision` and `TestLocalSandboxMountsTheProxyAndOverridesGOPROXY`. The error from both was `could not find a recognized version control system`. The same commit passed from an ordinary clone.

The local module proxy zips the repository with Go's module zip code, which looks for a `.git` directory. In a worktree `.git` is a file that points at the main checkout. `cs-sandbox build --local-sandbox` takes the same path, so it fails for anyone who works from a worktree.

To reproduce, run `git worktree add ../wt origin/main`, then `go test ./internal/cli/ -run TestLocalModuleProxy` in `../wt`.

Resolving the worktree's real git directory before zipping would fix it. `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` names it.
